stem.text: The extension of a copper wire is measured for different forces applied to the wire. A graph is plotted to show the variation of the force on the wire against extension. The maximum force is applied at point P.

stem.alt: Graph of force against extension with the vertical axis labelled force and the horizontal axis labelled extension, origin marked 0; a curve starts at the origin and rises, with points labelled T, S, R, Q and P marked along it.

A.text: Point R is the limit of proportionality.

B.text: The elastic potential energy of the wire at point S is given by the area under the graph between points T and S.

C.text: There is no plastic deformation between points Q and P.

D.text: The wire obeys Hooke's law up to a point between R and Q.
